record.original_question: If f in S, Baernstein has shown that Z 2π Z 2π iθ p |f (re )| dθ ≤ |k(reiθ )|p dθ, 0 < r < 1, 0 < p < ∞, 0 0 where k(z) is the Koebe function. Does the corresponding inequality hold for integral means of the derivatives at least for certain values of p? The best we can hope for is that it holds for p ≥ 13 because k′ (z) ∈ H p for p < 31 , and there exist functions f in S for which f ′ (z) does not belong to any H p . (An example is due to Lohwater, Piranian and Rudin [529]). For close-to-convex functions it was proved by MacGregor [541] that the result holds for p ≥ 1, and in fact the corresponding inequality holds for derivatives of all orders. (A. Baernstein)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of analytic and univalent functions $f$ on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ normalized by $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. Let $k(z)=z/(1-z)^2$ be the Koebe function (which belongs to $S$). For an analytic function $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and $0<r<1$, $0<p<\infty$, write the integral mean
$$M_p(r,g)=\int_0^{2\pi}|g(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta.$$
It is known (Baernstein) that
$$\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta\le\int_0^{2\pi}|k(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta$$
for every $f\in S$, every $0<r<1$ and every $0<p<\infty$.

Determine the set of values of $p$ for which the corresponding inequality for derivatives
$$\int_0^{2\pi}|f'(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta\le\int_0^{2\pi}|k'(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta$$
holds for every $f\in S$ and every $0<r<1$. In particular, does the inequality hold for all $p\ge 1/3$? (The threshold $1/3$ is the largest one can hope for, since $k'\in H^p$ exactly for $p<1/3$, while there exist $f\in S$ whose derivative $f'$ does not belong to any Hardy space $H^p$.)
artifact.status_search_result: Baernstein's integral-means inequality with the Koebe function as extremal in $S$ is well established. The analogous inequality for derivatives is known to hold for $p\ge 1$ in the close-to-convex subclass (MacGregor), but for the full class $S$ the question of whether the Koebe function is extremal for integral means of the derivative—particularly for $p\ge 1/3$—does not appear to be settled in the available literature; recent surveys still discuss it as an open extremal problem.

status_evidence.title: Integral Means Inequalities, Convolution, and Univalent Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Baernstein remarked that the analogous inequality for the derivative of a univalent function can be false at least for some range of parameters.
status_evidence.claim: The derivative analogue of Baernstein's theorem is not known in full generality and remains an open extremal problem.

status_evidence.title: Integral means, univalent functions and circular symmetrization
status_evidence.snippet: Baernstein established that the Koebe function is extremal for integral means of f in S.
status_evidence.claim: The original Baernstein theorem applies to f, not to f'.
